current.text: He came back from a torn Achilles much earlier than expected last season and finished 19th per game in limited minutes. He played 35 minutes a night in the playoffs.
After the Achilles he did not look fully like himself. He said he played at about 80 to 85%, and his rim finishing fell from 69 to 60.
He missed playoff Game 7 with knee inflammation from compensating for the Achilles. It is not chronic and needed no surgery. He is expected to arrive fully healthy.
Experts are not worried about the Achilles. The only open concern is the Game 7 knee issue. One expert rates that risk at about 1% and wants to hear at media day that he is fine.
Experts expect no minutes restriction. On back-to-backs they differ a little: the newest note says he will not sit them, and an earlier note says he may sit some.
Jaylen Brown has left Boston. Tatum is the number one option, with Paul George clearly second.
Experts expect a big usage season, with more usage than last season.
He is projected to start at forward and will play only some small-ball center.
His FG% should go up from last season, and one expert is fairly confident he returns to his best.
Experts call him good value at picks 6 to 8 and see a rank of 7 or 8 as fair. An ADP of 12 or 13 is too late. One expert would take him in round one, possibly ahead of Cade Cunningham.

Boston has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league, and three of them fall in the fantasy playoff window. The playoff schedule is 4-3-4 games through March 28, one game short of the maximum.
The expert expects Tatum to play the back-to-backs in the playoff window. Boston's back-to-backs mainly affect Paul George and Mitchell Robinson.

durable.text: Threes and points are clear league outliers on the strong side.
His rebounds and assists are well above other forwards.
Turnovers are his weakest category for a forward.
His weaknesses are blocks, steals and FG%.
He tore his Achilles in 2025-26. Before that injury he had a reputation as an iron man.

note: Yahoo and ESPN agree on him: values of 54 and 57 USD and a rank of 7 to 8. Experts call that fair or slightly cheap, so paying about 55 USD for a top 8 player is reasonable. He gives elite threes and points plus strong rebounds and assists for a forward, and turnovers are his main weakness, so he fits punt TO builds best. Early checks: the knee report at media day, whether his FG% gets back above 45%, and how Boston handles its 16 back-to-backs with him.
